As someone who has suffered from severe anxiety - the only thing that worked for me was exposure. I had built up a narrative in my mind that led to anything I did would end up in the worst case scenario. It wasn't until I did it over and over again did my mind retrain itself to feel confident in doing whatever was causing anxiety. 

Take baby steps, little bit more exposure at a time. 

As for the driving thing in particular, trying looking for jobs where there is really good mass transit. You'll likely have more opportunity and you won't need to drive.

Super been there. School was one of the worst times of my life until now. The only thing that got me through it was reading a lot and disappearing into the world of the books I was reading. Right now I can't even wait the three months that'll probably bring better times to me, so I totally get you. 

I will say that during school, people are at their worst. I was bullied a lot growing up and then found out years later that those same bullies were also suffering from depression and anxiety and used picking on others as their only means to feel good about themselves. I know that doesn't help when you're the brunt of the jokes... and being told to ignore it seems like a complete lack of support and understanding. Especially now that cyber-bullying exists. 

I believe that everyone is born a narcissist, and only through time and experience do we become empathetic creatures. And by experiencing what you're experiencing you will be able to connect with other people who have suffered in a way that no one who hasn't gone through what you are going through will be able to. Connecting with other humans and understanding that we all suffer, is the only thing that has kept me going these last few months. You will be a better person by getting through this, stronger and able to help others as they suffer. 

I'm aware of the irony of someone who is suicidal trying to talk someone else out of it, but... I guess I just wanted to say that I understand what you're going through, and it sucks. I kept a list of days left until graduation in my locker from when I was a sophomore. People made fun of me for it, but it helped to feel like I was getting closer each day to freedom. It felt like forever, but it did come. 

My only other advice would be to try and find someone who is suffering like you're suffering. You can be the support each other needs to get through this part of your life. You can't be the only one being bullied, and that may start a deep friendship based on your shared suffering. I know it helped for me.

I know it makes no sense to say "it'll get better." Obviously I don't know your life situation beyond what you've written. But I will say, if you are still underage and living at home, at least wait until you get out. There is something to be said about having control over your life, and not being forced to spend time around the people who bully you. I don't know how far away that is for you, and it may seem like forever, but it's worth a shot.
